args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying v2.3.1 to production, checkout-api failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. We rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service is healthy in all regions and the error rate is 0.2%. Next step: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's now passing health checks.

- **Rollback:** The broken release was v2.3.1, which was running in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all three regions are running it and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Staging warning:** The test build of v2.3.1 was also failing health checks in staging. It looks like it was deployed to production anyway.
- **Incident:** I opened a SEV2 incident for checkout-api, and the on-call engineer has been paged. It covers what failed, the rollback and the recovery numbers. As a next step, it says to find out why v2.3.1 failed before redeploying.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
